title: A response body may be written over time, and the streaming response ADR 0083 § 5 drew its line against was never built
scope:
the body a response carries while it is being sent, and the two doors onto it — a stream
that ends with its request, and one that outlives it. It changes nothing about a response this
server already holds in full, and nothing about the isolate a connection is, which
[0083](0083.md) decides.
validatedBy:
`crates/nvs-runtime/src/stream.rs`'s own cases, and
`crates/nvs-server/src/serve.rs`'s cases over `Answer`'s two arms.

summary.headline: A response body can be written over time, one chunk in flight at a time
summary.body:
A response is either a whole body with an exact length, as before, or a stream the handler
writes to while the connection sends it. Only the stream is chunked. The writer hands over one
chunk and waits until the connection has taken it before it may write the next, so a slow client
cannot make the server buffer an unbounded body. The stream ends with its request; a stream that
outlives the request is a separate door and is not this one.
